title: Caught on camera: Speeding Thar rams into scooter, 57-year-old dies
content:
The deceased was identified as Naval Sharma (Visuals-Social Media)

JAIPUR: A 57-year-old dairy operator was killed after his scooter was allegedly hit from behind by a speeding SUV in Jaipur's Sanganer area, police said on Monday. The accident took place on Saturday morning, while CCTV footage of the incident surfaced on Monday, police said. The deceased was identified as Naval Sharma, a resident of Buddhsinghpura in Sanganer. According to police, Sharma had left his home on his scooter around 6 am on Saturday to go to his dairy when a Mahindra Thar allegedly hit him from behind. The driver fled the spot after the accident, they said. Passersby informed the police, following which Sharma was taken to a hospital. He succumbed to his injuries during treatment. His body was handed over to his family on Sunday afternoon after a post-mortem examination at SMS Hospital. Police have formed two teams to trace the unidentified vehicle and arrest its driver.(With Agency Inputs)

title: Lt Gen Mohit Seth to be new GOC of White Knight Corps
content:
Maj Gen Mohit Seth took over as the General Officer Commanding (GOC) relieving Maj Gen SS Slaria who has moved to Headquarter Northern Command.

JAMMU: Lieutenant General Mohit Seth will take over as the new General Officer Commanding (GOC) of the Army’s Nagrota-based White Knight Corps (16 Corps) on Oct 1. He will replace Lt Gen P K Mishra, who will move to a new posting, officials said. In his distinguished military career spanning over three decades, Lt Gen Seth has served in key command and staff positions in J&K, the northeast, and at the Army HQ. He is currently the Commandant of the Indian Military Training Team in Bhutan. Lt Gen Seth previously was GOC of the Counter-Insurgency Force Kilo (Kilo Force), an elite formation of the Army’s Rashtriya Rifles tasked with anti-terror operations in north Kashmir. He has also served as the Indian Army Liaison Officer at the High Commission of India, United Kingdom.

title: Grounds in writing a must during arrests even in UAPA: Supreme Court
content: a bench of justices said a person must be provided with the grounds of arrest by the probe agency at the time of arrest in writing and its language understandable to the accused . the bench said this is applicable in all cases including under special laws - such as PMLA and UAPA .
